title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Aspen Group Employees
tiers.description: All Aspen Group Employees and any directors and staff of entities associated with Aspen Group including all syndicates and funds managed by Aspen Group, plus relevant consultants and contractors. Subject to the base rules: no trading in a Blackout Period without an exception or consent, no trading with material price-sensitive information, no short-term trading, no hedging/short selling/derivatives that limit risk exposure, and no margin lending or other secured financing.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling Aspen Group's activities (AASB 124), including any director, as listed in the Annual Report; includes retiring directors for 3 months after leaving. Together with 'other designated persons' (any employee designated in writing by the CEO or Company Secretary), must obtain prior written Trading Request Notice approval before any trade, at any time.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Aspen Group (a subset of Key Management Personnel). Trading Request Notices are addressed to the CEO, or to the Chairman in respect of non-executive directors, through the Company Secretary. Each director must notify the Company Secretary of any trading as soon as practicable and in any case no more than two days afterwards.

tiers.name: Related parties
tiers.description: Related parties as defined by section 228 of the Corporations Act, expressly including spouses, parents, children under 18 years, and trustees of a trust of which the employee or their family are beneficiaries. Employees and directors must ensure these persons are informed of the Policy and take reasonable steps to ensure compliance.

definitions.hedging_definition: An arrangement (including short selling Aspen Group Securities or Derivatives) that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk in relation to vested or unvested Aspen Group Securities (including any Aspen Group Securities granted as part of their remuneration).

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may impose further blackout periods at any time; the Chairman of the Board has discretion to make such decisions unilaterally. Confidentiality of such a decision is not addressed.

rules.detail: Unconditional ban with no clearance route, no vesting distinction and no tier distinction: it applies equally to vested and unvested securities and to every director and employee, unlike policies that permit hedging of vested unrestricted shares with approval.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees are prohibited from entering into an arrangement (including short selling Aspen Group Securities or dealing in Derivatives) that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk in relation to vested or unvested Aspen Group Securities (including any such Securities granted as part of their remuneration).

rules.detail: Derivatives (defined to include options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars) are named expressly; dealing in a Derivative that limits risk exposure over vested or unvested shares is banned outright for every director and employee, with no venue limitation.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees are prohibited from entering into an arrangement (including short selling Aspen Group Securities or dealing in Derivatives) that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk in relation to vested or unvested Aspen Group Securities

rules.detail: 'Trading' expressly includes 'any arrangement involving Hedging, Short Selling and Derivatives'. A derivative dealing that does not limit risk exposure (so falls outside Rule 5) is still Trading requiring a prior Trading Request Notice and approval.
rules.evidence: Any arrangement involving Hedging, Short Selling and Derivatives.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named separately, but a prepaid forward or similar structure is a 'Derivative' (forward contract) that limits risk exposure and so is expressly banned under Rule 5, over vested or unvested securities.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees are prohibited from entering into an arrangement (including short selling Aspen Group Securities or dealing in Derivatives) that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk in relation to vested or unvested Aspen Group Securities

rules.detail: Short selling is named expressly as an example of a prohibited risk-limiting arrangement.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees are prohibited from entering into an arrangement (including short selling Aspen Group Securities or dealing in Derivatives) that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named but fall within 'Derivatives' or 'other financial product' under section 1042A/761D of the Corporations Act referenced in the Securities definition; a CFD that limits risk exposure is banned under Rule 5, otherwise it is Trading requiring approval.
rules.evidence: Aspen Group Securities ... includes any interest in a Derivative or other financial product as defined in section 1042A of the Corporations Act

rules.detail: Unconditional ban on margin lending for every director and employee, with no clearance route, no vesting distinction and no carve-out for a lender's forced sale.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees must not enter into a margin lending arrangement or any other form of financing arrangement secured against Aspen Group Securities.

rules.detail: The prohibition on 'any other form of financing arrangement secured against Aspen Group Securities' necessarily bans granting any charge, lien or pledge over the shares, however structured.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees must not enter into a margin lending arrangement or any other form of financing arrangement secured against Aspen Group Securities.

rules.detail: The broadest possible scope: 'any other form of financing arrangement secured against Aspen Group Securities' is banned outright for every director and employee, with no Board-approval pathway, unlike policies that permit margin lending with clearance.
rules.evidence: Any form of financing arrangement secured against Aspen Group Securities.

rules.detail: No acquiring and disposing within 3 months or less from acquisition, other than under the Rule 1 qualifying exceptions.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees may not engage in short term trading in Aspen Group Securities i.e. acquiring Securities and disposing of them within 3 months or less from the date of acquisition (other than under the qualifying exceptions under Rule 1).

clearance.evidence: Directors and employees wishing to trade during the black-out period who consider that extraordinary circumstance apply, must obtain the consent of the Company Secretary before trading, however such consent will generally only be given for hardship cases.

clearance.approver: Chairman, CEO or their delegate (Trading Request Notice addressed to the CEO, or to the Chairman for non-executive directors, through the Company Secretary)
clearance.evidence: Approval is granted at the discretion of, and on such terms and conditions as determined, and advised in writing to the applicant, by the Chairman, CEO or their delegate. Approval may be refused at their discretion without being obliged to provide any reason.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as practicable, and in any case no more than two days afterwards
clearance.evidence: each director of Aspen Group must notify the Company Secretary as soon as practicable after any trading in Aspen Group Securities occurs, and in any case no more than two days afterwards.

short_term.evidence: acquiring Securities and disposing of them within 3 months or less from the date of acquisition (other than under the qualifying exceptions under Rule 1).

exceptions.evidence: An application for, or acquisition of, Aspen Group Securities under all Employee Share or Performance Rights Plans conducted by Aspen Group. This exception does not apply to trades after that original acquisition or application.

An acquisition of Aspen Group Securities under a Distribution Reinvestment Plan (DRP) provided: (i) the election to participate in the plan was made outside the black-out period and (ii) it was before you had any material price sensitive information.
Accepting a takeover bid or from selling Aspen Group Securities pursuant to a scheme of arrangement.
Transfers of already held Aspen Group Securities into a superannuation fund in which the employee is a beneficiary.
Participating in an offer controlled by the Board made to all securityholders such as a rights issue or Security Purchase Plan Scheme.
such consent will generally only be given for hardship cases. An example of a hardship case where consent to trade may be given is the case of a pressing financial hardship.

exemption_authority: None for the hedging/derivatives ban (Rule 5) or the margin lending/secured financing ban (Rule 6): both are unconditional prohibitions with no Board, Chairman or CEO discretion referenced anywhere in the Policy. The Chairman/CEO/delegate discretion under Rule 3 and the Company Secretary's hardship consent under Rule 1 apply only to ordinary share trading, not to the Rule 5 or Rule 6 prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees are prohibited from entering into an arrangement (including short selling Aspen Group Securities or dealing in Derivatives) that would have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk in relation to vested or unvested Aspen Group Securities (including any such Securities granted as part of their remuneration).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, there is no carve-out for vested, unrestricted securities and no clearance route at all - the purchased-put leg of a collar is banned for every director and employee regardless of vesting state.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and employees must not enter into a margin lending arrangement or any other form of financing arrangement secured against Aspen Group Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is broader than a margin-loan-only restriction and has no Board-approval pathway or disclosure regime, so the loan leg of a funded collar secured on the shares is prohibited outright for every director and employee.

bespoke_clauses.clause: What is a "Derivative"? Means, in relation to Aspen Group Securities, options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars as defined in section 761D of the Corporations Act.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy expressly recognises a 'collar' as a Derivative within the defined 'Aspen Group Securities', closing off any argument that an OTC collar structure falls outside scope.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All employees and directors must make sure that their spouses, children, parents and trustees are informed of this policy and to take reasonable steps to make sure they comply.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or related entity does not avoid the Rule 5 or Rule 6 prohibitions.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar is not possible under this Policy. Rule 5 unconditionally prohibits every director and employee from entering into any arrangement, including dealing in Derivatives (expressly defined to include collars, options and forward contracts), that would limit their exposure to risk in relation to either vested or unvested Aspen Group Securities - there is no clearance mechanism, Board discretion or tier-based carve-out for this prohibition, unlike the position for ordinary share trading under Rules 1 and 3. Separately, Rule 6 unconditionally bans margin lending or any other financing arrangement secured against Aspen Group Securities, again with no approval pathway, so the loan leg of a funded collar is also prohibited outright. Both prohibitions apply identically to Key Management Personnel, Directors and all other employees, and extend to related parties (spouses, parents, minor children, family trustees). With neither leg of the structure available and no exemption authority reaching either rule, a bank cannot offer this product to any Aspen Group director or executive under the current Policy.
